newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to issue first of zero coupon bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to issue first of zero coupon bonds.

text.p: Thailand's state-run Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) plans to issue its first zero coupon bonds on May 2, a central bank official said on Thursday.
The bonds to be auctioned will be worth between 500 million baht and one billion baht ($19.2-$38.5 million) and have a seven-year maturity, the official told reporters.
The official said the bonds issued by PLMO will be guaranteed by the finance ministry.
The PLMO was set up last month by the government as part of its rescue plan to help shore up battered property sector which has been hit by liquidity crunch.
The government had said earlier that it planned to float up to 100 billion baht, seven-year zero-coupon bonds to raise funds for its refinancing to property projects that face short-term cashflow.

Some property firms have had a hard time repaying loans and are faced with a glut of space. Their problems have had a knock-on effect on financial institutions who have lent them billions of dollars for their projects.
